hypothesis: Pair the two physical faces at the first crest with the two straight midpoint-locus portions in B, encouraging the false assumption that constant normal offsets meet in a sharp crest rather than a circular arc.
primary_math_proof: While the wheel contacts a straight face, its midpoint is on a parallel line at perpendicular distance r. At a convex crest, contact stays at the crest while the center travels on a radius-r circular arc connecting the offset face lines. At a concave valley, simultaneous contact with both faces switches at the intersection of the offset lines, giving a sharp valley. Thus the locus has rounded crests and sharp valleys: E alone. A rounds both, B has sharp crests and rounded valleys, C plateaus, D has both sharp. The four marks cover one existing crest/its candidate local counterpart only; they do not add paths, remove rounding, change wheel radius, add contact points or alter the grey track.
